card.name: Chhau
card.era: Roots in indigenous dance and martial practices; UNESCO-inscribed 2010
card.tagline: Eastern Indian masked martial dance of epics and ritual
card.profile: Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance combining martial, tribal and folk traditions, found in three regional styles: Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj (Odisha), the first two using masks (Wikipedia). It enacts episodes from the Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas, local folklore and abstract themes, and is intimately connected to the spring festival Chaitra Parva (UNESCO). Its movement vocabulary includes mock combat (khel), stylized gaits of birds and animals, and movements based on village chores; it is traditionally performed by male troupes at night to reed pipes (mohuri, shehnai) and drums.
card.insight: Chhau was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi established a National Centre for Chhau Dance at Baripada, Odisha (Wikipedia).
